metadata.name: 青云研语 · 保研英语面试题库

question.en: Please introduce yourself briefly.
question.zh: 请用英语简单介绍一下你自己

thinking: 1min = 我是谁 + 我做过什么 + 我想研究什么。
2min = 我是谁 + 我有什么能力 + 我的研究兴趣是怎么形成的 + 我是什么样的人。
3min = 一个完整的“研究型学生画像”：学术基础 + 科研轨迹 + 代表性经历 + 研究兴趣 + 个人特质 + 读研目标。

phrases.en: That experience changed the way I think about...
For graduate study, I hope to...

en: Good morning, professors. My name is Li Zhexuan and I am an undergraduate student majoring in Computer Science at Hangzhou Dianzi University.
I rank within the top five percent of my major and have received several provincial and national awards.

During my undergraduate study, I participated in projects involving computer vision, robotics, and LLM-based agents. One representative project was an industrial automotive repair robot. I was mainly responsible for bolt detection, and I later participated in building an agent workflow based on ReAct and tool calling. This work also led to my first-author EI conference paper.
These experiences gradually developed my interest in AI agents and intelligent systems, especially task planning, tool use, feedback, and collaboration.
I hope to receive systematic research training in graduate school and further explore this field. Thank you.
2 min｜展开版
Good morning, professors. My name is Li Zhexuan, and I am an undergraduate student majoring in Computer Science at Hangzhou Dianzi University.
I rank within the top five percent of my major and have built a solid foundation in computer science. I have also received several scholarships and awards during my undergraduate study.
My main research experience has been around computer vision, robotics, and intelligent agents. I have worked on projects in medical imaging, industrial robotics, and LLM-based agent systems.

One project that influenced me a lot was an automotive repair robot. I was initially responsible for bolt detection and developed a lightweight attention module to improve the detection of small targets. This work later became my first-author EI conference paper. After that, I also participated in building the agent workflow, where we connected planning, tool use, and execution feedback.

This experience gradually changed the way I think about AI. Instead of only improving a single model, I became more interested in how an intelligent system can perceive the environment, make decisions, use tools, and learn from feedback.
Outside academics, I have studied the violin for about fifteen years and served as a deputy leader of a student orchestra. I really enjoy working with others toward a common goal.
For graduate study, I hope to receive systematic research training and further explore AI agents and intelligent systems, especially in real-world applications.
Thank you.
3 min｜标准版
Good morning, professors. My name is Li Zhexuan, and I am an undergraduate student majoring in Computer Science at Hangzhou Dianzi University.

Academically, I rank within the top five percent of my major. During my undergraduate study, I have maintained a strong interest in computer science and artificial intelligence, and I have received several scholarships and competition awards.

My research experience has mainly focused on computer vision, robotics, and intelligent agents. I have participated in projects involving medical image analysis, industrial robots, and LLM-based agent systems. These experiences gave me opportunities not only to study algorithms, but also to work on real problems with real constraints.

One representative experience was an automotive repair robot. I was initially responsible for the visual detection module. Because the robot had to detect small bolts under complex lighting conditions, I analyzed the failure cases and developed a lightweight attention module to improve detection performance. The related work later became my first-author EI conference paper.

But what influenced me even more came later. I also participated in the agent side of the system. We turned several robot operations into callable tools and connected task planning, tool use, and execution feedback.

That experience gradually changed my research interest. At first, I mainly cared about how to make an individual model perform better. Later, I became more interested in a broader question: how can we build an intelligent system that can understand a task, make decisions, interact with tools, and adjust its behavior based on feedback?

This is why I am now particularly interested in AI agents and intelligent systems. I hope to explore these problems in real-world settings, especially systems that need perception, planning, and interaction.

I would also describe myself as someone who enjoys learning by doing. When I encounter a problem, I like to understand why it happens, test different solutions, and gradually improve the system. I think this habit has helped me a lot in both research and engineering projects.

Outside academics, music is another important part of my life. I have studied the violin for about fifteen years and served as a deputy leader of a student orchestra. Playing in an orchestra has taught me a lot about collaboration, communication, and working toward a common goal.

For graduate study, I hope to receive more systematic research training. In particular, I want to improve my ability to identify meaningful research problems, design convincing experiments, and eventually turn research ideas into intelligent systems that can work reliably in the real world.
Thank you.
zh: 身份 → Top 5% → 维修机器人/LECA → 一作论文 → 从模型转向完整智能系统 → 研究生阶段系统训练。

question.en: Could you introduce your hometown?
question.zh: 请介绍一下你的家乡

thinking: 先真正“介绍杭州” → 风景与文化 → 美食 → 数字经济 → 最后一句个人感受

phrases.en: What I like about the city is...

en: I am from Hangzhou, the capital of Zhejiang Province, and I am also studying there now.
Hangzhou is best known for West Lake, and places like Hefang Street, the Grand Canal, and the Qiantang River are also very representative of the city.
It is also famous for Longjing tea and local food such as Dongpo pork and xiaolongbao.
At the same time, Hangzhou has a strong digital economy and a very active internet and technology industry.
I really like this mix of tradition and innovation.
Growing up in Hangzhou has made me energetic, adaptable, and open to change.
At the same time, it has also taught me to slow down, reflect, and recharge when I need to.
zh: 我的家乡是杭州，也是浙江省省会，我现在也在杭州读大学。
杭州最有代表性的当然是西湖，像河坊街、古运河和钱塘江也都很有杭州特色。
杭州还以龙井茶和东坡肉、小笼包等地方饮食闻名。
与此同时，杭州的数字经济和互联网科技产业也很活跃。
我很喜欢这种传统与创新并存的感觉。
在杭州长大让我变得更有活力、更能适应变化，也更愿意接受新事物。
同时，这座城市也让我学会在需要的时候慢下来、思考和恢复状态。

question.en: Could you introduce your university?
question.zh: 请介绍一下你的本科院校

thinking: 学校是谁 → 在哪、历史 → 学科特色 → 学校文化/培养特色 → 校园生活 → 最后一句自己的感受

en: I study at Hangzhou Dianzi University, usually called HDU. It is located in Hangzhou and was founded in 1956.

HDU is especially known for its strengths in electronic information and computer science. It has also been closely connected with China's electronics and information industry throughout its history, and this background has shaped its strong engineering culture.

Another important feature of HDU is its emphasis on practical learning and innovation. Students are encouraged to take part in academic research，competitions and  engineering projects, so there are many opportunities to apply what we learn in class to real problems.
Campus life is also quite active, with many student clubs, sports activities, and cultural events.
Overall, HDU has provided me with a solid foundation in computer science and many opportunities to explore beyond the classroom. I think these experiences have prepared me well for further study.
zh: 我就读于杭州电子科技大学，通常简称杭电。
学校位于杭州，始建于1956年，是一所以电子信息特色突出、计算机等相关学科见长的研究教学型大学，办学历史也一直和我国电子信息产业联系比较紧密。
杭电还有很强的实践氛围，学生比较早就有机会参加竞赛、工程项目和科研。
校园生活也很丰富，有很多社团和文体活动。
对我来说，杭电既打下了专业基础，也给了我很多课堂之外真正去尝试和成长的机会。

question.en: What are your strengths and weaknesses?
question.zh: 请介绍你的优点和缺点

thinking: 两点优势 → 第一，坚持 → 学琴长期训练 + 科研遇难题不放弃 → 第二，务实 → 缺点，过早抠细节 → 用优先级和时间限制改进

en: I would describe my strengths in two aspects.

First, I am persistent. I have played the violin for many years, and this experience taught me the value of steady practice. The same habit also helps me in study and research. When I meet a difficult problem, I usually keep working on it step by step.

Second, I am quite practical and action-oriented. In research and projects, I usually focus on whether an idea can actually be implemented and tested, rather than only discussing it at the conceptual level.
As for my weakness, I sometimes focus too much on details before the overall structure is clear.
I am improving this by setting priorities and time limits before I start a task.
zh: 我觉得我的优点主要有两个方面。
第一，我比较有坚持性。长期学习小提琴让我养成了持续练习、逐步改进的习惯，这种习惯也会带到学习和科研中。遇到比较困难的问题时，我通常愿意继续做下去，一步一步把问题解决。
第二，我做事情比较务实，尤其是在科研和项目中。我不仅会考虑一个想法在理论上是否合理，也会关注它能不能真正实现、验证，并根据实际结果继续改进。
至于缺点，我有时候会在整体框架还没有完全确定之前，就花比较多时间去打磨一些细节。现在我会通过提前确定优先级和时间限制来改善这个问题，先解决最重要的部分，再逐步完善细节。

question.en: Could you tell us something about your family?
question.zh: 请介绍一下你的家庭

thinking: 先回答“家里有谁、分别做什么” → 再用1–2句说家庭氛围和对我的影响

phrases.en: There are four people in my family...

en: There are four people in my family: my father, my mother, my younger sister, and me.
My father works as a financial director at a company.
My mother is retired now.
My younger sister is in the fifth grade, so there is quite a big age difference between us.
We live in Hangzhou.
My family atmosphere is relaxed and supportive.
My parents usually give me space to make my own decisions, but they also give practical advice when I need it.
I think this has helped me become more independent and responsible.
zh: 我家里有四个人：爸爸、妈妈、妹妹和我。
爸爸在一家公司担任财务总监，妈妈现在已经退休。
妹妹还在读五年级，所以我和她年龄差比较大。
我们一家都生活在杭州。
家里的氛围比较轻松，也很支持我的选择。
父母通常会让我自己做决定，需要的时候再给我一些现实的建议。
我觉得这种方式让我更独立，也让我更愿意为自己的选择负责。

question.en: What are your interests and hobbies?
question.zh: 你的兴趣爱好是什么

thinking: 小提琴是主线：音乐本身的美和感受 → 合奏简单带过 → 跑步作为放松方式；不要硬扯科研

en: My main hobby is playing the violin.
I have learned it for about fifteen years.
So it has become an important part of my life.
I think the violin is a good way to express myself.
Sometimes it is hard to describe my feelings in words.
But I can express them through music.
I also enjoy practicing by myself.
It helps me relax and slow down.
And I like performing for other people.
When people enjoy my performance, I feel very happy.
It gives me a strong sense of achievement.
I also enjoy ensemble playing.
When different parts fit together, the result can be much richer than any single part alone.
It made me realize that music is not only about expressing yourself.
It is also about listening to others and finding your place in the whole piece.
Besides music, I like running.
It is a simple way for me to relax.
When I feel stressed or mentally tired, going for a run usually helps me clear my mind.
zh: 我最主要的爱好是小提琴，已经学习大约十五年，所以音乐一直是我生活里很重要的一部分。
我最喜欢的是小提琴本身的音色，以及音乐能够表达很多难以用语言说清楚的情绪。
我也很喜欢合奏，不同声部真正配合起来时，整体会比任何一个单独声部更丰富。
除此之外我也喜欢跑步。
它对我来说是一种很简单的放松方式，压力大或者脑子很乱的时候，出去跑一会儿通常就会舒服很多。

question.en: What is one of your most memorable experiences at university?
question.zh: 大学期间最难忘的一段经历是什么

thinking: 用量化投资竞赛讲“陌生领域 + 短时间学习 + 团队协作 + 做出完整结果”

phrases.en: I had to learn very quickly...
What I learned from this was...

en: One of my most memorable experience was participating in a  quantitative investment competition.
I chose to take part because I was very interested in finance and quantitative investing.
However, I did not have much background in finance at that time.
In our team, I mainly worked on the quantitative models and coding.
My teammates from finance mainly read research reports and studied possible investment strategies.
Then we discussed the strategies together, tested different ideas, and kept improving our solution.
The competition was quite intensive, so I had to learn a lot of new financial knowledge in a short time.
In the end, we won a provincial first prize.
More importantly, this experience gave me more confidence in myself.
It showed me that even in an unfamiliar field, I can learn quickly, work with people from different backgrounds, and solve the problem step by step.
zh: 我大学里一段很难忘的经历，是参加一次量化投资竞赛。
它特别的地方在于，金融一开始并不是我熟悉的领域，但我们只有几天时间去理解问题、查资料、分工，再把学到的东西变成一套完整方案。
我必须很快进入一个陌生领域，并把新的领域知识和自己已有的技术能力连接起来。
整个过程节奏很快，但团队一直在讨论、测试和改进，最后获得了省级一等奖。
这段经历让我确认了一件事：面对陌生问题，我能够先抓住结构，再快速学习，并和团队在时间压力下把事情做完整。

question.en: Who is the most unforgettable person you met at university?
question.zh: 大学期间最难忘的人是谁

thinking: 导师 → 一次真实卡住的经历 → 老师如何帮我重新看问题 → 我后来改变了什么

phrases.en: Since then, I have tried to...

en: The most unforgettable person I met at university is one of my research supervisors.
I remember one experience very clearly.
At that time, I was working on a music recommendation project.
I had tried several ideas, but none of them worked well, so I felt quite lost.
One evening, my supervisor called me and discussed the problem with me.
I was only an undergraduate student, but he still took my ideas very seriously.
He listened patiently and helped me look at the problem from a different perspective.
He did not simply tell me what to do.
Instead, he asked me questions and encouraged me to rethink some of my assumptions.
What impressed me most was his patience and his attitude toward students.
Even when my ideas were immature, he was willing to discuss them with me seriously.
He gave me more confidence in doing research.
That is why he is still one of the most unforgettable people I have met at university.
zh: 大学里让我印象最深的人，是我的一位科研导师。
有一次我做音乐推荐项目时一直没有进展，尝试了几种方案以后，我开始怀疑是不是整个方向都有问题。
老师晚上还专门和我通话，帮我重新梳理问题，并建议我先跳出原来的方法，看看包括扩散模型在内的其他建模思路。
真正让我印象深刻的不是某一个具体技术，而是老师让我学会：科研卡住时，不要只是沿着原路线继续硬调，而要退一步去质疑自己的假设。
后来我遇到问题时，也会更主动地先重新审视问题本身。

question.en: What kind of books do you often read?
question.zh: 你经常阅读什么类型的书

thinking: 技术类书籍 → 举一个真实例子 → 技术书能帮助我系统理解一个领域 → 和论文相比，书能把基础、经典方法和工程实践串起来 → 书凝聚了前人的知识和经验 → 虽然部分内容可能会过时，但基础仍然有价值 → AI时代更需要书来建立完整的知识框架

phrases.en: What I value about this kind of book is...

en: I mainly read technical books, especially books about AI and algorithms.
One example is Deep Learning Recommender Systems 2.0 by Wang Zhe.
I like this kind of  book because they give me a more systematic view of how a field develops.
Papers are useful for learning specific new ideas, while a good technical book can connect basic concepts, classical methods, and engineering practice.
It also contains the knowledge and experience that researchers and engineers have built up over many years.
Some parts may become outdated, but the basic ideas and classical methods can still give me a solid foundation.
I think this is especially valuable now, because AI tools can answer many isolated questions very quickly, but they do not automatically give you a coherent map of a field.
zh: 我平时主要阅读技术类书籍，尤其是人工智能和算法相关的书。
比如王喆的《深度学习推荐系统2.0》。
我喜欢这类书，因为它们可以让我更系统地了解一个领域是如何发展起来的。
论文很适合用来学习一些具体的新思想，而一本好的技术书可以把基础概念、经典方法和工程实践联系起来。
同时，书中也包含了很多研究人员和工程师多年积累下来的知识和经验。
虽然其中的一些内容可能会随着技术发展而过时，但基础思想和经典方法仍然可以帮助我打下扎实的基础。
我觉得这一点在现在尤其有价值，因为AI工具可以很快回答很多零散的问题，但它们并不会自动帮你建立起一个完整、连贯的领域知识框架。

question.en: Please describe one of your most unforgettable competition experiences.
question.zh: 请描述一次最难忘的竞赛经历

thinking: 和Q07共用同一段量化投资故事，减少记忆负担；
讲述路线：为什么参加—我做了什么—怎么合作—最后收获什么

en: My most memorable competition was a quantitative investment competition.
I chose to take part because I was very interested in finance and quantitative investing.
However, I did not have much background in finance at that time.
In our team, I mainly worked on the quantitative models and coding.
My teammates from finance mainly read research reports and studied possible investment strategies.
Then we discussed the strategies together, tested different ideas, and kept improving our solution.
The competition was quite intensive, so I had to learn a lot of new financial knowledge in a short time.
In the end, we won a provincial first prize.
More importantly, this experience gave me more confidence in myself.
It showed me that even in an unfamiliar field, I can learn quickly, work with people from different backgrounds, and solve the problem step by step.
zh: 我最难忘的一次竞赛是一场量化投资竞赛。
我当时对金融和量化投资很感兴趣，所以选择参加了这个比赛。
但那时我的金融基础并不多。
在团队中，我主要负责量化模型和代码实现。
金融专业的队友主要负责阅读研报，并研究可能的投资策略。
然后我们会一起讨论策略、测试不同想法，并不断改进方案。
比赛节奏比较紧张，所以我需要在很短的时间内学习很多新的金融知识。
最后，我们获得了省级一等奖。
更重要的是，这次经历让我对自己更有信心了。
它让我意识到，即使面对一个陌生领域，我也能够快速学习、和不同背景的人合作，并一步一步把问题解决掉。

question.en: What is your favorite English-language movie?
question.zh: 你最喜欢的英语电影是什么

thinking: 《星际穿越》 → 第一印象很震撼 → 真正吸引我的是探索未知 → 面对不确定仍然寻找答案 → 科学与情感并存 → 为什么喜欢

phrases.en: What stayed with me most was...
For me, it is the kind of film that...

en: My favorite English-language movie is Nolan's Interstellar.
The first time I watched it, I was deeply impressed by the music, the visual effects, and the huge scale of the story.
But what I like most about the movie is its spirit of exploration.
The characters face many things they cannot predict, but they still try to understand the unknown and find a way forward.
I also like how the film combines scientific ideas with human emotions, especially family, responsibility, and difficult choices.
For me, it is not only visually powerful, but also the kind of film that makes me keep thinking after it ends.
zh: 我最喜欢的英语电影是《星际穿越》。
第一次看时，音乐、画面和宏大的故事给我很强的震撼。
但我真正喜欢的是它所体现的探索精神。
电影中的人物面对很多无法预测的事情，但他们仍然试图理解未知，并寻找继续前进的方法。
我也很喜欢它把科学想象和人的情感结合在一起，比如家庭、责任和艰难的选择。
对我来说，它不只是视觉上很震撼，也是一部看完之后还会让人继续思考的电影。

question.en: Why did you choose our university?
question.zh: 你为什么选择我们学校

thinking: 具体匹配点 → 导师/方向 → 我能带来什么

phrases.en: The main reason is research fit.
This connects well with my previous experience in...

en: I chose your university mainly because of research fit.
I am interested in [research area], and I have read about the work of Professor [name] and the group.
Their focus on [specific problem] connects well with my experience in computer vision, robotics, and AI agents.
I also want stronger training in [method or skill].
At the same time, I can bring hands-on experience in building and evaluating real AI systems.
So my choice is based on a concrete match, not only on the university's reputation.
zh: 我选择贵校最主要的原因是研究匹配。
我对[研究方向]感兴趣，也了解过[导师姓名]老师及团队在[具体问题]上的工作，这和我过去在计算机视觉、机器人以及AI Agent方面的经历能够衔接。
我也希望在[方法或能力]上接受更系统的训练。
同时，我可以带来真实AI系统构建和评测方面的实践经验。
因此，我的选择不是只看学校名气，而是看具体的研究和培养是否适合我。

question.en: Why did you choose this major?
question.zh: 你为什么选择这个专业

thinking: 抽象知识 → 可运行系统 → 项目验证

phrases.en: Project work made this interest stronger.
That combination is what keeps me interested in...

en: I chose Computer Science because it connects abstract ideas with systems that can actually run.
Courses such as Machine Learning taught me how models learn from data, while Operating Systems and Compiler Principles helped me understand what happens underneath.
Project work made this interest stronger.
In the repair-robot project, an algorithm only became useful when it could work with planning, tool calls, and feedback.
That combination of theory, engineering, and real-world impact is what keeps me interested in Computer Science.
zh: 我选择计算机，是因为它能把抽象的思想变成真正可以运行的系统。
机器学习让我理解模型怎样从数据中学习，操作系统和编译原理又让我看到更底层的机制。
项目经历进一步验证了这种兴趣。
在维修机器人项目里，算法只有和规划、工具调用、执行反馈连起来以后才真正有价值。
理论、工程和现实影响之间的这种结合，是我想继续学计算机的原因。

question.en: How would you evaluate your performance today?
question.zh: 请评价一下你今天的表现

thinking: 承认紧张 → 说清优点 → 一点可改进

phrases.en: I was a little nervous at first, but...
One thing I could improve is...

en: I think my performance was generally stable.
I was a little nervous at the beginning, but I became more focused as the interview continued.
I tried to answer the questions directly and explain my own work clearly.
There are still places where I could be more concise or precise, especially when answering an unexpected question.
Overall, I am glad that I was able to show my real experience and way of thinking.
zh: 我觉得今天整体发挥比较稳定。
刚开始会有一点紧张，但随着面试进行，我逐渐更专注。
我尽量直接回答问题，也尽可能把自己的工作讲清楚。
当然还有一些地方可以更简洁、更准确，尤其是面对没有准备过的问题时。
总体上，我比较满意的一点是，能够把自己的真实经历和思考方式展示出来。

question.en: Could you tell us about your plans for postgraduate study?
question.zh: 请谈谈你的研究生阶段规划

thinking: 第一年补基础 → 中期做研究 → 后期形成独立能力

en: In the first stage of graduate study, I want to strengthen my foundation and learn the research methods used by the group.
I also hope to read important papers and reproduce solid baselines instead of rushing into a new idea.
After that, I want to focus on one research problem and build a complete cycle from question, method, experiment, to analysis.
By the later stage, I hope I can define problems more independently and produce work that is both technically sound and useful in real settings.
zh: 研究生前期，我希望先补强基础，熟悉课题组常用的研究方法，并通过阅读重要论文和复现可靠baseline建立判断力，而不是急着追一个新点子。
之后，我希望围绕一个具体问题形成完整的研究闭环，从问题、方法、实验到分析都能做扎实。
到后期，我希望自己能够更独立地提出问题，并做出既技术可靠、又对真实场景有价值的工作。

question.en: What is the most important quality for a postgraduate student?
question.zh: 你认为研究生最重要的素质是什么

thinking: 结论 → 原因 → 我的理解

phrases.en: I think the most important quality is...

en: I think the most important quality is the ability to keep learning independently.
Graduate research is different from coursework because many problems do not have a standard answer.
You need to read, test ideas, accept negative results, and change direction when the evidence is different from what you expected.
Persistence is important, but persistence without reflection can also waste time.
So for me, good graduate students should be able to learn continuously and update their judgment based on evidence.
zh: 我认为研究生最重要的素质是持续自主学习的能力。
科研和课程不同，很多问题没有标准答案，需要自己读文献、做实验、接受负结果，也要在证据和预期不一致时及时调整。
坚持当然重要，但如果没有反思，盲目坚持也可能浪费时间。
所以我理解的优秀研究生，是能够不断学习，并根据证据更新自己判断的人。

question.en: What are your research interests?
question.zh: 你的研究兴趣是什么

thinking: 一个总方向 → 两个具体问题 → 与经历连接

phrases.en: This connects with my previous experience in...

en: My current interest is reliable intelligent systems, especially AI agents and multimodal decision-making in real-world tasks.
I am interested in two questions.
First, how can an agent choose and use tools based on intermediate feedback instead of following a fixed script?
Second, how can we evaluate when such a system is reliable enough to act, and when it should stop or ask for help?
These questions connect well with my previous experience in robotics, autonomous-driving diagnosis, and multimodal models.
zh: 我目前比较感兴趣的是真实场景中的可靠智能系统，尤其是AI Agent和多模态决策。
我比较关注两个问题：第一，智能体怎样根据中间反馈选择和调用工具，而不是只按固定流程执行；第二，我们怎样判断一个系统什么时候足够可靠可以行动，什么时候应该停止或请求帮助。
这些问题和我之前在机器人、自动驾驶诊断以及多模态模型方面的经历比较一致。

fallbacks.fallback: We want to know whether the system can still make a safe and reasonable decision when the situation changes.

question.en: Do you intend to pursue a PhD?
question.zh: 你是否有攻读博士学位的意向

thinking: 开放但不空喊 → 依据研究体验决定

phrases.en: If I find a problem that I truly want to continue exploring,...

en: I am open to pursuing a PhD, but I do not want to give a fixed answer before I have experienced graduate research in depth.
For me, a PhD should come from a real interest in a research question and the willingness to work on it for several years, not simply from wanting a higher degree.
During my master's study, I hope to build stronger research ability first.
If I find a problem that I truly want to continue exploring, I would seriously consider a PhD.
zh: 我对读博是开放的，但在真正深入经历研究生科研之前，我不想给一个过于确定的答案。
对我来说，读博应该来自对某个研究问题真正长期的兴趣，而不是单纯追求更高学历。
硕士阶段我希望先把科研能力做扎实。
如果之后遇到一个我确实愿意继续投入几年去研究的问题，我会认真考虑攻读博士。

question.en: Why did you choose graduate school instead of working or studying part-time?
question.zh: 为什么选择读研，而不是直接工作或边工作边读

thinking: 现在的能力边界 → 研究需要系统训练 → 读研是最合适路径

phrases.en: What I want to learn next is...
So for me, graduate study is...

en: I considered this question from the perspective of what I want to learn next.
My project experience taught me how to build systems, but it also showed me the limits of my current knowledge.
I can implement an idea, but I still need stronger training in research design, evaluation, and deeper theory.
A full-time graduate program gives me the time and environment to focus on these skills.
So for me, graduate study is not a delay before working.
It is the most direct way to prepare for the kind of work I want to do.
zh: 我主要从“下一步真正需要学什么”来考虑这个问题。
项目经历让我学会了做系统，但也让我看到自己目前的能力边界：我可以实现一个想法，但在研究设计、评测方法和更深入的理论上还需要系统训练。
全日制研究生阶段能提供更集中的时间和环境。
因此，对我来说，读研不是把工作往后拖，而是为未来想做的事情做更直接的准备。

question.en: Please introduce your major.
question.zh: 请介绍一下你的专业

thinking: 计算机研究什么 → 我学了什么 → 它训练了什么思维

en: My major is Computer Science and Technology.
It covers both how computation works and how we build reliable software systems.
My coursework includes algorithms, operating systems, compiler principles, software engineering, machine learning, and data mining.
What I value most is that the major trains both abstraction and implementation.
You need to understand a principle, but you also need to make it work under real constraints.
That combination has shaped the way I approach research and engineering problems.
zh: 我的专业是计算机科学与技术。
它既研究计算本身的原理，也关注怎样构建可靠的软件和智能系统。
我的课程包括算法、操作系统、编译原理、软件工程、机器学习和数据挖掘等。
我最看重的是这个专业同时训练抽象思维和实现能力：既要理解原理，也要让它在真实约束下运行。
这种训练很大程度上影响了我处理科研和工程问题的方式。

question.en: What is your favorite course, and how did you perform in it?
question.zh: 请介绍你最喜欢的课程以及你的表现

thinking: 课程为什么难 → 我怎么学 → 对我的影响

phrases.en: One course that influenced me a lot was...

en: One course that influenced me a lot was Operating Systems.
It contains a lot of concepts, and some of them are quite abstract and easy to confuse, such as processes and threads, or paging and segmentation.
So I reorganized the whole course with mind maps and connected the concepts instead of memorizing them separately.
This not only helped me get a good grade, but also taught me to understand the overall structure before going into details.
zh: 对我影响很大的一门课是操作系统。
这门课内容很多，而且有不少概念比较抽象、名字也很相近，比如进程和线程、分页和分段，很容易混淆。
后来我把整门课重新整理成了思维导图，把不同知识点之间的关系和区别串起来，而不是零散地记忆。
这个过程不仅让我最后取得了比较好的成绩，也让我养成了先梳理结构、再理解细节的学习习惯。

question.en: How well do you understand artificial intelligence?
question.zh: 你对人工智能了解多少

thinking: 定义 → 能做什么 → 当前边界

phrases.en: Strong capability does not automatically mean...

en: My understanding of AI is still developing, but I see it as a set of methods that allow machines to learn patterns, make predictions, generate content, or take actions from data and feedback.
Deep learning has greatly improved perception and generation, and foundation models are now connecting language, vision, tools, and actions.
At the same time, strong capability does not automatically mean reliability.
In real applications, we still need good data, clear evaluation, safety constraints, and human oversight.
zh: 我对人工智能的理解还在不断加深。
我把它看成一组让机器能够从数据和反馈中学习模式、进行预测、生成内容或采取行动的方法。
深度学习大幅提升了感知和生成能力，而基础模型正在把语言、视觉、工具和行动进一步连接起来。
但能力强并不等于可靠。
在真实应用中，我们仍然需要好的数据、清晰的评测、安全约束以及必要的人类监督。

fallbacks.fallback: We want to understand why the model makes this decision.
The model can still work well when the input changes.

question.en: Please explain a theory or mechanism that you are familiar with.
question.zh: 请介绍一个你熟悉的理论或机制

thinking: 是什么 → 怎么做 → 为什么有效 → 用在哪里 → 我的理解/实践

en: I am quite familiar with the attention mechanism.
The basic idea is that a model should focus more on important information instead of treating everything equally.
It usually calculates an importance score for different parts of the input and then uses these scores to combine the information.
Attention is a key component of Transformer models, and it is also widely used in computer vision and multimodal learning.
I have also used a similar idea in my own work, where I designed a channel attention module to help the model focus on more useful visual features.
zh: 我比较熟悉注意力机制。
核心思想是：不同信息的重要程度不同，模型应该把更多注意力放在重要信息上。
它通常先计算不同部分的重要性分数，再根据这些分数对信息进行加权组合。
注意力机制是 Transformer 的核心，也广泛用于视觉和多模态任务。
我自己的研究中也使用过类似思想，通过通道注意力让模型更关注有用的视觉特征。

question.en: Could you briefly introduce your competition experience?
question.zh: 请简要介绍你的竞赛经历

thinking: 不报菜名 → 按能力归类 → 两个代表例子

phrases.en: My competition experience mainly falls into...

en: My competition experience mainly falls into two types.
One is engineering and system building.
For example, I served as the project leader in the Service Outsourcing Competition, where our team won a national third prize.
The other is mathematical modeling.
I won a provincial first prize in the China Undergraduate Mathematical Contest in Modeling and later received an Honorable Mention in MCM.
These competitions trained different skills, but they all taught me how to learn quickly, divide work, validate results, and deliver under time pressure.
zh: 我的竞赛经历主要可以分成两类。
一类是工程系统类，比如服务外包大赛，我担任项目负责人，团队最终获得全国赛企业命题类三等奖。
另一类是数学建模，我获得过全国大学生数学建模竞赛浙江省一等奖，后来在美赛中获得Honorable Mention。
这些比赛训练的技能不同，但共同让我学会了快速学习、团队分工、验证结果以及在时间压力下完成交付。

question.en: How do you usually read a research paper?
question.zh: 你通常如何阅读一篇论文

thinking: 先问题后细节 → 带问题读 → 复现/验证

phrases.en: I usually read a paper in several passes.
If the paper is important to my work,...

en: I usually read a paper in several passes.
First, I look at the title, abstract, figures, and conclusion to understand the problem and the main claim.
Then I read the method and experiments with specific questions: what is really new, what baseline is used, and whether the evidence supports the claim.
If the paper is important to my work, I go back to the details and sometimes reproduce part of it.
I also use AI tools to explain difficult passages, but I always return to the original paper and verify the key points myself.
zh: 我通常会分几遍读论文。
第一遍先看标题、摘要、图和结论，弄清它解决什么问题、核心结论是什么。
第二遍带着问题看方法和实验：真正的新东西是什么、和什么baseline比较、证据是否支持结论。
如果这篇论文和我的工作很相关，我会再回到细节，必要时做部分复现。
我也会用AI辅助解释难句，但关键结论一定会回到原文自己核对。

question.en: How do you think computer science and AI will develop in the future?
question.zh: 你认为未来计算机或人工智能会如何发展

thinking: 趋势 → 难点 → 我关注什么

phrases.en: I think AI will move from... to...
But I do not think the future is only about...
That is also why I am interested in...

en: I think AI will move from models that mainly generate content to systems that can perceive, reason, use tools, and act in the real world.
Multimodal models and agents are important parts of that change.
But I do not think the future is only about making models larger.
Evaluation, data quality, efficiency, safety, and controllability will become more important as AI is used in higher-stakes tasks.
That is also why I am interested in reliable agents rather than capability alone.
zh: 我认为AI会从主要负责生成内容的模型，逐渐发展为能够感知、推理、调用工具并在真实世界中行动的系统，多模态和Agent会是其中很重要的方向。
但未来不只是把模型做得更大。
随着AI进入更高风险的任务，评测、数据质量、效率、安全和可控性会越来越重要。
这也是为什么我现在更关注可靠的智能体，而不只是单纯追求能力。

question.en: What have you learned from your research experience?
question.zh: 你从科研经历中学到了什么

thinking: 科研不是调参 → 问题/证据/边界

phrases.en: The biggest lesson I learned is...
A negative result is still useful if...

en: The biggest lesson I learned is that research is not just about getting a better number.
You first need a clear question.
Then you need evidence that actually answers that question.
In my earlier work, I sometimes focused too quickly on improving a model.
Later I learned to look at failure cases, compare baselines, and ask what the result really proves.
I also learned that negative results are useful if they help us reject a weak idea or find a problem in the experimental setup.
zh: 我从科研中学到最重要的一点是，科研不是只把指标做高。
首先要有一个清楚的问题，然后要有真正能回答这个问题的证据。
我早期有时会太快进入“怎么把模型提升”的思路，后来逐渐学会看失败样本、做baseline比较，并追问实验结果到底证明了什么。
我也开始接受负结果，因为它可以帮助我们排除一个不好的想法，或者发现实验设计中的问题。

question.en: What difficulty did you encounter during your research?
question.zh: 你在科研过程中遇到过什么困难

thinking: 具体困难 → 我的动作 → 结果/反思

phrases.en: I did not treat it as...

en: In the repair-robot project, one difficult problem was screw detection under complex lighting.
The targets were small, and reflections or similar structures could easily cause false detections.
I did not treat it as a single “model problem.
” I checked the data, failure cases, and feature behavior, then tested different improvements.
This process led me to design LECA, a lightweight channel-attention module.
The experience taught me that a useful improvement should come from understanding the failure pattern, not from adding complexity blindly.
zh: 在维修机器人项目里，一个比较难的问题是在复杂光照下检测螺栓。
目标本身很小，反光和相似结构又容易造成误检。
我没有把它只当成“换个模型”的问题，而是去检查数据、失败样本和特征表现，再逐步测试不同改进。
这个过程最终让我设计了轻量级通道注意力模块LECA。
它让我明白，有价值的改进应该来自对失败模式的理解，而不是盲目增加复杂度。

question.en: If we gave you an offer, would you definitely accept it?
question.zh: 如果我们给你 offer，你一定会来吗

thinking: 只做真实承诺 → 第一志愿可直接说 → 否则说明选择标准

phrases.en: If this is my confirmed first choice,...
If I am still comparing programs,...

en: If this program is my confirmed first choice, I would answer directly: yes, I would accept the offer and make the commitment seriously.
If I am still comparing programs, I would not make a false promise.
I would say that I am very interested because of the specific research fit, and that I will make a responsible decision within the required time.
I think an offer is a commitment from both sides, so honesty is more important than saying what sounds safest in the moment.
zh: 如果这个项目确实是我已经确定的第一志愿，我会直接回答：是的，我会接受，并认真履行承诺。
如果当时我仍在比较不同项目，我不会为了过关做虚假承诺。
我会说明自己为什么对这里非常感兴趣，以及会在规定时间内根据研究匹配和长期发展认真作出决定。
我认为offer是双方的承诺，所以诚实比临场说一句最“安全”的话更重要。

question.en: Which other universities or programs have you applied to?
question.zh: 你还申请了哪些学校或项目的预推免

thinking: 按“当前真实状态”简短列举 → 不讲流水账 → 最后说自己的选择标准；这是预推免，不是夏令营

phrases.en: I would keep the status clear...
My choices are mainly based on...

en: I have applied to several graduate programs in Computer Science and AI through the current recommendation-admission process.
I would answer this question with the current facts at the time of the interview, because the status of each application changes quickly.
I would briefly name the programs I have applied to and make the status clear, such as submitted, invited to interview, or already completed.
My choices are not random.
I mainly compare research direction, supervisors, training style, and long-term development.
For your program, I would then explain the specific reason why it is a strong fit for me.
zh: 我还申请了几所计算机和人工智能相关项目的预推免。
这道题面试时一定要按当天的真实状态回答，因为各个申请的进度变化很快。
我会简要列出自己申请了哪些项目，并把“已提交、收到面试、已经参加”等状态说清楚，不混在一起。
我的选择并不是随机投递，主要会看研究方向、导师匹配、培养方式和长期发展。
列完事实后，我会把重点拉回贵项目，说明它为什么对我有具体吸引力。

question.en: What was the biggest difficulty you faced during recommended admission or research, and how did you handle it?
question.zh: 在保研或科研中你遇到了什么困难，如何应对

thinking: 压力来源 → 拆分任务 → 调整 → 反思

phrases.en: One difficulty I have faced is...
I broke the problem down into...

en: One difficulty I have faced is having several important tasks at the same time, such as research, application preparation, and coding practice.
My first reaction used to be to think about everything together, which made the workload feel larger than it really was.
I now break the work into smaller tasks, decide what is time-sensitive, and set a clear minimum goal for each day.
This does not remove the pressure, but it makes the next action clear and helps me keep moving instead of waiting for the perfect state.
zh: 我遇到过的一个现实困难，是科研、申请材料和机考准备等重要任务同时出现。
以前我容易把所有事情一起想，结果会觉得工作量比实际更大。
现在我会把任务拆小，先判断什么有明确截止时间，再给每天设置一个清楚的最低完成目标。
这样并不会让压力消失，但会让下一步行动变得明确，也能避免一直等“状态完美”才开始做。

question.en: What would you do if you were not successful this time?
question.zh: 如果这次保研失败，你会怎么做

thinking: 情绪稳定 → 复盘 → 继续目标

phrases.en: Of course I would be disappointed, but...

en: Of course I would be disappointed, but I would not treat one result as a final judgment on my ability.
I would review where I was not competitive enough, continue improving my research and technical skills, and prepare for the next realistic path to graduate study or work.
The specific route may change, but my longer-term goal of becoming stronger in computer science and AI would not.
I think the important thing is to turn the result into information for the next decision.
zh: 如果没有成功，我当然会失落，但不会把一次结果看成对自己能力的最终判断。
我会复盘自己在哪些方面竞争力不足，继续提升科研和技术能力，并准备下一条现实可行的升学或工作路径。
具体路线可能改变，但我希望继续在计算机和人工智能方向成长的长期目标不会改变。
我更愿意把结果当成下一次决策的信息。

question.en: What do you think of deep learning?
question.zh: 谈谈你对深度学习的理解

thinking: 是什么 → 为什么强 → 局限

en: Deep learning is a way of learning useful representations through multi-layer neural networks.
Its strength is that it can learn complex patterns directly from large amounts of data instead of relying only on hand-designed features.
It has been very successful in vision, language, speech, and many other areas.
But it also has limitations.
Models can be data-hungry, hard to interpret, and sensitive to distribution shifts.
So I think the key question is not only how powerful a model is, but also when we can trust its behavior.
zh: 深度学习可以理解为利用多层神经网络自动学习有效表示的方法。
它的优势是能够从大量数据中学习复杂模式，而不完全依赖人工设计特征，因此在视觉、语言、语音等领域都取得了很大成功。
但它也有明显局限，例如需要大量数据、解释困难，并可能对分布变化比较敏感。
所以我认为重要的不只是模型有多强，还包括我们什么时候能够信任它的行为。

fallbacks.fallback: The model should also work well on data it has never seen before.

question.en: What do you think of artificial intelligence?
question.zh: 谈谈你对人工智能的理解

thinking: 能力层次 → 当前变化 → 人的责任

phrases.en: The recent change I find most interesting is...
At the same time, we still need...

en: I see artificial intelligence as a broad field that tries to build systems capable of perception, learning, reasoning, generation, or action.
The recent change I find most interesting is that these abilities are being connected.
A model can now understand multiple types of input, call tools, and complete longer tasks.
But AI is still a tool built and evaluated by people.
Its outputs depend on data, objectives, and system design.
So human judgment and responsibility are still essential, especially in high-stakes applications.
zh: 我把人工智能理解为一个很广的领域，目标是让系统具备感知、学习、推理、生成或行动等能力。
我觉得最近最有意思的变化，是这些能力正在被连接起来：模型可以理解多种输入、调用工具，并完成更长链条的任务。
但AI仍然是由人设计和评测的工具，它的输出受到数据、目标和系统设计的影响。
因此，尤其在高风险场景里，人类判断和责任仍然不可替代。

fallbacks.fallback: We want to understand why the model makes this decision.
The system can still work well when the input or environment changes.

question.en: Please introduce your student innovation project.
question.zh: 请介绍一下你的学生创新项目

thinking: 问题 → 核心思路 → 当前进展 → 不夸大

en: My student innovation project focuses on diagnosing failures in autonomous-driving systems.
The motivation is that when a driving system makes a bad decision, the root cause may come from perception, planning, control, or the interaction between them.
Our idea is to use structured diagnostic agents to collect evidence from different modules and then make a traceable diagnosis.
I am especially interested in active evidence collection and calibrated abstention.
The project is still in progress, so I treat these as research hypotheses that need to be tested, not as finished conclusions.
zh: 我的学生创新项目主要研究自动驾驶系统的故障诊断。
动机是：当自动驾驶出现错误决策时，根因可能来自感知、规划、控制，也可能来自不同模块之间的交互。
我们的思路是让结构化诊断Agent从不同模块收集证据，再形成可追溯的诊断。
我尤其关注主动获取证据和“证据不足时拒答”的机制。
项目仍在进行中，所以我会把这些当作需要实验验证的研究假设，而不是已经完成的结论。

question.en: What are the innovative points of this project?
question.zh: 这个学生创新项目的创新点是什么

thinking: 创新不是堆Agent → 三个可检验点

phrases.en: The main idea is not simply to...
I would describe the innovation as...

en: The main idea is not simply to use several agents.
I would describe the innovation as three testable points.
First, the system actively decides what evidence to request instead of reading a fixed set of logs.
Second, it reasons across perception, planning, and control, so it can distinguish a local error from a cross-module failure.
Third, it is allowed to abstain when the evidence is not strong enough.
The key is whether these designs improve diagnosis accuracy and evidence cost compared with simpler baselines.
zh: 这个项目的创新点并不是“用了多个Agent”本身。
我更愿意把它归纳成三个可以实验验证的点：第一，系统主动决定还需要什么证据，而不是只读固定日志；第二，它跨感知、规划和控制做责任定位，区分局部错误和跨模块故障；第三，在证据不足时允许拒答。
真正关键的是，这些设计能否相对于更简单的baseline提升诊断准确性，并控制获取证据的成本。

question.en: Please introduce your paper briefly.
question.zh: 请简要介绍你的论文

thinking: 问题 → LECA → 实验 → 价值

en: My first-author paper is about screw detection in difficult industrial scenes.
Small screws can be easily missed under reflections, uneven lighting, and complex backgrounds.
I designed a lightweight channel-attention module called LECA.
It extends lightweight cross-channel interaction with additional statistical descriptors, so the network can use richer information when recalibrating feature channels.
We evaluated it in our detection task and observed improvements with a small parameter cost.
The paper was published in an IEEE-indexed conference.
zh: 我的第一作者论文主要研究复杂工业场景下的螺栓检测。
小螺栓在反光、光照不均和复杂背景下比较容易漏检。
我设计了一个轻量级通道注意力模块LECA，在轻量跨通道交互的基础上加入额外统计描述，让网络在重新校准特征通道时使用更丰富的信息。
我们在检测任务中进行了实验，在较小参数开销下取得了提升。
论文已经在IEEE会议发表并检索。

question.en: What are the innovative points of your paper?
question.zh: 你的论文创新点是什么

thinking: 现有方法缺什么 → 我加什么 → 为什么轻量

en: The main innovation is in how channel information is summarized.
Lightweight attention methods are efficient, but a single pooled descriptor may lose useful statistics.
LECA keeps lightweight cross-channel interaction and adds several learnable statistical descriptors, including information related to feature variation and activation strength.
These descriptors are not hard rules.
They are signals that the network can learn to use.
The goal is to improve channel calibration without introducing a heavy attention block.
zh: 这篇论文的主要创新在于通道信息怎样被汇总。
轻量级注意力方法效率很高，但如果只使用单一的池化描述，可能会丢掉一些有用统计信息。
LECA保留轻量的跨通道交互，同时加入与特征变化和激活强度相关的可学习统计描述。
这些统计量不是人工硬规则，而是供网络学习利用的信号，目标是在不引入重型注意力模块的情况下改善通道校准。

question.en: What was your contribution to this project?
question.zh: 你在学生创新项目中的贡献是什么

thinking: 我负责什么 → 我实际做了什么 → 团队边界

phrases.en: I keep the boundary clear between...

en: I am responsible for the overall research design and the diagnostic framework of the project.
I helped define the main hypotheses, designed the comparison between fixed evidence collection, greedy strategies, and agent-based diagnosis, and worked on the experimental pipeline.
I also take part in checking whether the environment can produce valid evidence.
I try to keep the boundary clear: some infrastructure and system components are team work, while my main responsibility is the research question, diagnostic method, and evaluation design.
zh: 我主要负责这个项目的整体研究设计和诊断框架，包括定义核心假设、设计固定证据、greedy策略和Agent诊断之间的对比，以及推进实验流程。
我也会参与检查实验环境能否产生可信证据。
我会明确区分个人和团队贡献：部分基础设施和系统组件是团队合作，我的主要责任是研究问题、诊断方法和评测设计。

question.en: What was your main contribution to the paper project?
question.zh: 你在论文项目中的主要贡献是什么

thinking: 一作贡献 → 方法 → 实验 → 写作

phrases.en: At the same time, the project was collaborative.

en: As the first author, my main contribution was the design and evaluation of LECA.
I analyzed the failure patterns in screw detection, developed the module, and carried out the main comparison and ablation experiments.
I also organized the results and took the lead in writing and revising the paper.
At the same time, the project itself was collaborative, so I would not describe the data collection, hardware system, or every engineering component as my independent work.
zh: 作为第一作者，我的主要贡献是LECA的设计与验证。
我分析了螺栓检测中的失败模式，完成模块设计，并负责主要的对比和消融实验，同时整理结果并主导论文写作和修改。
这个项目本身是团队合作，因此我不会把数据采集、硬件系统或所有工程组件都说成是我独立完成的。

question.en: What challenges did you encounter in the project?
question.zh: 你在项目中遇到了哪些挑战

thinking: 感知 → 系统接口 → 研究证据

phrases.en: There were three types of challenges.

en: There were three types of challenges.
First, perception was difficult because the targets were small and the scene had reflections and confusing structures.
Second, system integration was difficult because detection results had to be converted into coordinates and tool actions correctly.
Third, from a research perspective, we had to separate a real improvement from an accidental result.
I dealt with these problems through failure-case analysis, interface checks, controlled experiments, and repeated testing rather than relying on one model change.
zh: 这个项目的挑战大致有三类。
第一是感知，目标小、反光多、相似结构容易干扰；第二是系统集成，检测结果必须正确转成坐标和工具动作；第三是研究证据，我们要区分真实改进和偶然结果。
我主要通过失败样本分析、接口检查、受控实验和重复测试来处理这些问题，而不是把希望全部放在一次模型修改上。

question.en: What are the current limitations of the project?
question.zh: 这个项目目前有什么缺点或局限

thinking: 主动讲边界 → 下一步

en: The first limitation is generalization.
The system has mainly been tested in a specific repair setting, so performance cannot be assumed in other vehicles or environments.
The second limitation is end-to-end reliability.
A good detector does not guarantee that coordinates, tool calls, and physical actions will all be correct.
The third limitation is evaluation coverage.
We still need more failure cases and clearer system-level metrics.
I would address these issues with broader testing, structured failure logs, and stricter end-to-end evaluation.
zh: 第一类局限是泛化。
目前系统主要在特定维修场景中测试，不能直接假设它在其他车辆和环境中同样可靠。
第二类是端到端可靠性：检测准确并不等于坐标、工具调用和实际动作都会正确。
第三类是评测覆盖，我们还需要更多失败场景和更清晰的系统级指标。
下一步我会通过更广泛测试、结构化失败日志以及更严格的端到端评测来改进。

question.en: Could you introduce Changsha?
question.zh: 请介绍一下长沙

thinking: 省会身份 → 代表性文化/景点 → 当代城市气质 → 一句个人印象

en: Changsha is the capital of Hunan Province.
It is a city with a strong cultural identity.
Yuelu Mountain and Yuelu Academy are two well-known places, and they reflect the city's long connection with education and scholarship.
Changsha is also famous for its lively food culture and relaxed atmosphere.
At the same time, it is a modern city with active industries, media, and technology.
What I find interesting is the contrast between its historical side and its very young, energetic urban culture.
zh: 长沙是湖南省省会，城市文化辨识度很强。
岳麓山和岳麓书院都很有代表性，也体现了这座城市和教育、学术传统之间很深的联系。
长沙的饮食文化和生活氛围也很有名。
与此同时，它也是一座现代城市，在产业、媒体和科技方面都很活跃。
我觉得它很有意思的一点，是历史感和非常年轻、热闹的城市气质同时存在。

question.en: Could you introduce Shanghai?
question.zh: 请介绍一下上海

thinking: 国际化大城市 → 金融/科技/高校资源 → 城市景观与文化 → 为什么对学生有吸引力

phrases.en: one of China's most international cities
From a student's point of view,...

en: Shanghai is one of China's most international cities and an important center for finance, technology, and higher education.
The city has very different sides.
Areas such as the Bund show its modern history, while Pudong represents its fast development and global business environment.
Shanghai also has many strong universities, research institutes, and technology companies.
From a student's point of view, I think the biggest attraction is the density of opportunities.
You can meet people from different fields, learn about new ideas quickly, and connect academic work with real industries.
zh: 上海是中国最国际化的城市之一，也是金融、科技和高等教育的重要中心。
它的城市层次非常丰富，外滩体现了近现代城市历史，浦东则更能代表快速发展和国际商业环境。
上海还集中了很多高校、科研机构和科技企业。
从学生角度看，我觉得它最大的吸引力是机会密度很高，可以接触不同领域的人和新想法，也更容易把学校里的学习和真实产业联系起来。

question.en: Could you introduce Nanjing?
question.zh: 请介绍一下南京

thinking: 古都身份 → 历史文化 → 高校科研 → 城市给人的整体感觉

phrases.en: one of China's well-known historic cities
What I like about the city is...

en: Nanjing is the capital of Jiangsu Province and one of China's well-known historic cities.
It has many important cultural and historical sites, such as the city wall and the area around the Qinhuai River.
At the same time, Nanjing is also a major center for higher education and research.
It has many universities and a strong engineering and technology base.
What I like about the city is that history and modern student life are very close to each other.
It feels academically active without losing its historical character.
zh: 南京是江苏省省会，也是中国很有代表性的历史文化名城。
南京有很多重要的历史文化景观，比如明城墙、秦淮河一带。
与此同时，南京也是高等教育和科研资源非常集中的城市，有很多高校，也有很强的工程和科技基础。
我比较喜欢它的一点，是历史和现代大学生活离得很近，既有很强的学术氛围，又保留了很鲜明的城市历史感。

question.en: Could you introduce Xi’an?
question.zh: 请介绍一下西安

thinking: 古都与历史地位 → 代表性景观 → 高校/航空航天/电子信息 → 古老与硬科技并存

phrases.en: one of the most important ancient capitals

en: Xi'an is the capital of Shaanxi Province and one of the most important ancient capitals in Chinese history.
It is known for places such as the city wall and the Terracotta Warriors, so the historical atmosphere is very strong.
At the same time, Xi'an is also an important city for higher education, aerospace, electronics, and engineering.
Many universities and research institutes are located there.
I think this combination is very distinctive.
It is a city with thousands of years of history, but it also has a strong connection with modern science and technology.
zh: 西安是陕西省省会，也是中国历史上最重要的古都之一。
西安以古城墙、兵马俑等景观闻名，所以城市的历史感非常强。
与此同时，西安也是高等教育、航空航天、电子信息和工程领域的重要城市，有很多高校和科研机构。
我觉得这种组合很有特点：一边是几千年的历史积淀，一边又和现代科技、硬科技产业联系得很紧。

question.en: Which programming language are you most comfortable with, and why?
question.zh: 你擅长哪种编程语言，为什么

thinking: C++ → 用过它做什么 → 为什么是扎实基础 → 不说“一种语言解决所有问题”

phrases.en: I do not think one language is best for every task.

en: I am most comfortable with C and C++, especially for algorithmic problems.
I used C++ in the CCF CSP assessment and received a score of 240.
I like it because it gives me clear control over data structures, memory, and performance, and it also helps me understand what happens under higher-level abstractions.
Of course, I do not think one language is best for every task.
In AI projects I also use the tools and languages that fit the ecosystem, but C++ is my strongest foundation.
zh: 我最熟悉的是C/C++，尤其在算法题和系统基础方面。
我参加CCF CSP认证时使用C++，取得了240分。
我喜欢它是因为对数据结构、内存和性能的控制比较直接，也能帮助我理解高层抽象之下发生了什么。
当然，我不认为一种语言适合所有任务。
在AI项目里我也会根据生态使用其他工具和语言，但C++是我最扎实的编程基础。

question.en: What do you enjoy most about doing research?
question.zh: 科研中你最享受的是什么

en: What I enjoy most about research is the moment when a vague problem gradually becomes clearer.
At the beginning, I may only have an intuition.
Then I read, run experiments, and check whether the evidence supports it.
Sometimes the result is different from what I expected, and that is also interesting.
I enjoy this process of asking a question, testing it, and updating my understanding.
zh: 科研中我最享受的，是一个模糊的问题逐渐变清楚的过程。
刚开始时，我可能只有一个直觉。
之后我会读文献、做实验，再看证据是否真的支持这个想法。
有时候结果和预期不一样，这反而也很有意思。
我喜欢这种提出问题、验证问题，再不断更新自己理解的过程。

tags: P01 专业选择与学术动机

question.en: What is your understanding of your prospective supervisor's research area?
question.zh: 你怎样理解意向导师的研究领域

en: I chose your university mainly because of research fit.
I am interested in [research area], and I have read about the work of Professor [name] and the group.
Their focus on [specific problem] connects well with my experience in computer vision, robotics, and AI agents.
I also want stronger training in [method or skill].
At the same time, I can bring hands-on experience in building and evaluating real AI systems.
So my choice is based on a concrete match, not only on the university's reputation.
zh: 我选择贵校最主要的原因是研究匹配。
我对[研究方向]感兴趣，也了解过[导师姓名]老师及团队在[具体问题]上的工作，这和我过去在计算机视觉、机器人以及AI Agent方面的经历能够衔接。
我也希望在[方法或能力]上接受更系统的训练。
同时，我可以带来真实AI系统构建和评测方面的实践经验。
因此，我的选择不是只看学校名气，而是看具体的研究和培养是否适合我。

tags: P01 专业选择与学术动机

question.en: Why do you want to pursue graduate study?
question.zh: 你为什么希望读研

en: I considered this question from the perspective of what I want to learn next.
My project experience taught me how to build systems, but it also showed me the limits of my current knowledge.
I can implement an idea, but I still need stronger training in research design, evaluation, and deeper theory.
A full-time graduate program gives me the time and environment to focus on these skills.
So for me, graduate study is not a delay before working.
It is the most direct way to prepare for the kind of work I want to do.
zh: 我主要从“下一步真正需要学什么”来考虑这个问题。
项目经历让我学会了做系统，但也让我看到自己目前的能力边界：我可以实现一个想法，但在研究设计、评测方法和更深入的理论上还需要系统训练。
全日制研究生阶段能提供更集中的时间和环境。
因此，对我来说，读研不是把工作往后拖，而是为未来想做的事情做更直接的准备。

tags: P01 专业选择与学术动机

question.en: What connections do you see among your research projects?
question.zh: 你如何看待研究项目之间的联系

en: Although my projects dealt with different topics, they all allowed me to explore related questions beyond the classroom.

In each project, I gained hands-on experience in collecting information and analyzing evidence, but each one also helped me deepen my understanding of the same broader issue from a different perspective.
Together, they taught me to connect theoretical knowledge with real-world problems and gradually confirmed my interest in pursuing a clearer research direction.
zh: 虽然我的几个项目涉及不同主题，但它们都让我能够在课堂之外继续探索相互关联的问题。
在每个项目中，我都获得了信息收集和证据分析方面的实践经验；与此同时，每个项目也让我从不同角度加深了对同一个宽泛问题的理解。
这些经历共同教会我把理论知识与现实问题联系起来，也逐渐进一步确认了我想研究的方向。
研究生阶段，我希望以过去在这些项目中的经验为基础继续发展，而不是把它们视为彼此割裂的经历。

tags: P01 专业选择与学术动机

question.en: What strengths do you have that are relevant to this field?
question.zh: 你有哪些与本领域相关的优势

en: One strength of mine is persistence.
I have played the violin for many years, and the same habit helps me in study and research.
When a problem is difficult, I can stay with it and improve step by step.
I also like turning ideas into working systems instead of stopping at a concept.
One weakness is that I sometimes spend too much time refining details before the main structure is fixed.
I am improving this by setting priorities and time limits, and by asking myself what is really necessary at each stage.
zh: 我的一个优势是比较能长期坚持。
我学小提琴很多年，这种习惯也影响了我的学习和科研：遇到难题时，我愿意一点一点把它做下去。
另外，我比较喜欢把想法真正做成可以运行的系统。
我的不足是有时会在整体框架还没完全确定时，就花太多时间打磨细节。
现在我会先定优先级和时间上限，并不断问自己“这个阶段最需要解决的是什么”。

tags: P01 专业选择与学术动机

question.en: Could you briefly introduce your undergraduate major?
question.zh: 请简要介绍一下你的本科专业

en: My major is Computer Science and Technology.
It covers both how computation works and how we build reliable software systems.
My coursework includes algorithms, operating systems, compiler principles, software engineering, machine learning, and data mining.
What I value most is that the major trains both abstraction and implementation.
You need to understand a principle, but you also need to make it work under real constraints.
That combination has shaped the way I approach research and engineering problems.
zh: 我的专业是计算机科学与技术。
它既研究计算本身的原理，也关注怎样构建可靠的软件和智能系统。
我的课程包括算法、操作系统、编译原理、软件工程、机器学习和数据挖掘等。
我最看重的是这个专业同时训练抽象思维和实现能力：既要理解原理，也要让它在真实约束下运行。
这种训练很大程度上影响了我处理科研和工程问题的方式。

tags: P01 专业选择与学术动机

question.en: Why do you want to switch to a different major?
question.zh: 你为什么希望转换专业

en: My decision is not a sudden change.
I gradually developed an interest in the new field through elective courses, independent reading, and practical experience.
I was particularly drawn to the way it approaches questions that I had already encountered in my undergraduate studies.
I therefore began to explore the field beyond the classroom and deepen my understanding of its basic ideas.
zh: 这个决定并不是突然作出的。
我通过选修课程、自主阅读和实践经历，逐渐对新的领域产生了兴趣。
我尤其被它处理本科阶段已经接触过的一些问题的方式所吸引。
因此，我开始在课堂之外继续探索这个领域，并加深对其基本理念的理解。

question.en: Why do you want to pursue this area as your research direction?
question.zh: 你为什么希望将这个方向作为研究领域

en: My current interest is reliable intelligent systems, especially AI agents and multimodal decision-making in real-world tasks.
I am interested in two questions.
First, how can an agent choose and use tools based on intermediate feedback instead of following a fixed script?
Second, how can we evaluate when such a system is reliable enough to act, and when it should stop or ask for help?
These questions connect well with my previous experience in robotics, autonomous-driving diagnosis, and multimodal models.
zh: 我目前比较感兴趣的是真实场景中的可靠智能系统，尤其是AI Agent和多模态决策。
我比较关注两个问题：第一，智能体怎样根据中间反馈选择和调用工具，而不是只按固定流程执行；第二，我们怎样判断一个系统什么时候足够可靠可以行动，什么时候应该停止或请求帮助。
这些问题和我之前在机器人、自动驾驶诊断以及多模态模型方面的经历比较一致。

My name is Zhexuan Li.
I am a Computer Science student at Hangzhou Dianzi University.
My GPA is 4.
589 out of 5.
0, and I rank 19th out of 465 students.
My main project experience is in computer vision, robotics, and AI agents.

That work led to a first-author paper.
These experiences made me interested in reliable intelligent systems, especially AI agents that can perceive, plan, use tools, and learn from feedback.

zh: 各位老师好，我叫黎哲轩，来自杭州电子科技大学计算机科学与技术专业。
本科期间，我主要做过计算机视觉、机器人和AI Agent相关项目。
在工业维修机器人项目中，我负责视觉检测，并设计了轻量级注意力模块LECA，相关工作形成了一篇第一作者论文。
这些经历让我逐渐关注真实场景中的可靠智能系统，尤其是能够感知、规划、调用工具并根据反馈调整的AI Agent。

question.en: Why would you like to work with this supervisor?
question.zh: 你为什么希望跟随这位导师学习

en: I looked into the professor's research through recent papers and project introductions.
The way the research connects careful analysis with meaningful questions stood out to me.
This work fits my current interests and is relevant to my previous experience in project-based learning.
I believe it would allow me to use what I have already learned in information analysis and benefit from guidance in research design and academic reasoning.
zh: 我通过近期论文和项目介绍进一步了解了这位老师的研究。
这些研究把严谨分析与有意义的问题联系起来，这一点尤其吸引我。
老师的研究与我的学术兴趣高度一致，也与我过去在项目式学习方面的经历相关。
我相信，这能让我以过去在信息分析方面的经验为基础继续发展，并从研究设计和学术推理方面的指导中受益。

question.en: Do you have any questions for us?
question.zh: 你有什么问题想问我们

en: Yes, thank you.
I have learned more about the program through its curriculum and research information, and its emphasis on student development stood out to me.
Since the training fits my current interests and fits the direction I want to explore, I would like to ask how first-year students usually become involved in ongoing research.
I would also like to know how students benefit from guidance in developing independent research questions.
zh: 有，谢谢。
我已经通过培养方案和研究信息进一步了解了这个项目，其中对学生成长的重视尤其吸引我。
由于这里的培养与我的学术兴趣高度一致，也符合我希望发展的方向，我想请问一年级学生通常如何参与正在开展的研究。
我也想了解，学生如何从形成独立研究问题的指导中受益。

question.en: What kind of relationship would you like to build with your supervisor?
question.zh: 你希望与导师建立怎样的关系

en: I hope to build a relationship based on open communication, mutual respect, and growing independence.
At the beginning, I would like to benefit from guidance in research design and academic thinking, especially when learning how to define a worthwhile question.
At the same time, I should bring a solid foundation in independent learning and responsible work habits rather than wait passively for instructions.
zh: 我希望与导师建立一种以坦诚沟通、相互尊重和逐步独立为基础的关系。
刚开始时，我希望能够从研究设计和学术思考方面的指导中受益，尤其是学习如何提出值得研究的问题。
同时，我也应该具备自主学习和认真负责方面的扎实基础，而不是被动等待指令。
我希望以过去在自我管理学习方面的经验为基础继续发展，而导师的研究也符合我希望发展的方向。

question.en: How do you usually read academic papers?
question.zh: 你通常如何阅读学术论文

en: I usually read a paper in several passes.
First, I look at the title, abstract, figures, and conclusion to understand the problem and the main claim.
Then I read the method and experiments with specific questions: what is really new, what baseline is used, and whether the evidence supports the claim.
If the paper is important to my work, I go back to the details and sometimes reproduce part of it.
I also use AI tools to explain difficult passages, but I always return to the original paper and verify the key points myself.
zh: 我通常会分几遍读论文。
第一遍先看标题、摘要、图和结论，弄清它解决什么问题、核心结论是什么。
第二遍带着问题看方法和实验：真正的新东西是什么、和什么baseline比较、证据是否支持结论。
如果这篇论文和我的工作很相关，我会再回到细节，必要时做部分复现。
我也会用AI辅助解释难句，但关键结论一定会回到原文自己核对。

question.en: How do you balance coursework, research, student work, and extracurricular activities?
question.zh: 你如何平衡课程、科研、学生工作和课外活动

en: I first separate fixed deadlines from tasks that can move.
Coursework and application deadlines get a clear time block, while research is divided into smaller weekly goals.
I also keep one or two activities, such as music or exercise, because they help me stay stable rather than simply filling every hour with work.
When several tasks conflict, I decide what matters most for the current stage and accept that not everything can be optimized at the same time.
zh: 我会先把有硬性截止时间的事情和可以调整的事情分开。
课程和申请节点会固定时间，科研则拆成较小的周目标。
我也会保留音乐或运动这类活动，因为它们能帮助我保持稳定，而不是把每个小时都塞满。
任务冲突时，我会判断当前阶段什么最重要，也接受不可能同时把所有事情都做到最优。

tags: P03 课程学习与学术成长

question.en: Which academic journals do you usually read in your field?
question.zh: 你平时关注本领域的哪些学术期刊

en: I follow several influential journals in my field, but I do not try to read every article they publish.
I read with a clear purpose and select papers related to the questions I am currently studying.
Review articles help me build a solid foundation in an unfamiliar topic, while recent research helps me keep up with developments in my field.
I also compare ideas and findings across papers instead of relying on a single source.
zh: 我会关注本领域一些有影响力的期刊，但不会试图阅读其中发表的每篇文章。
我会带着明确目的阅读，选择与当前学习问题相关的论文。
综述文章能够帮助我在陌生主题上打下扎实基础，近期研究则帮助我跟进本领域的发展。
我也会比较不同论文的观点和发现，而不是依赖单一来源。

question.en: How do you keep up to date with developments in your field and current affairs?
question.zh: 你如何跟进本领域的最新发展和时事

en: I use a combination of academic journals, university or institutional websites, and reliable news sources.
I read with a clear purpose and first check who produced the information, what evidence it uses, and whether other reliable sources support it.
For academic topics, I compare ideas and findings across papers rather than depend on a single study.
This helps me identify gaps in my understanding and keep up with recent developments in my field.
zh: 我会综合使用学术期刊、高校或专业机构网站以及可靠的新闻来源。
我会带着明确目的阅读，首先检查信息由谁发布、使用了什么证据，以及是否得到其他可靠来源的支持。
对于学术主题，我会比较不同论文的观点和发现，而不是依赖某一项研究。
这帮助我发现自己理解中的缺口，并跟进本领域的最新发展。

I also compared its ideas and findings with those of other papers and used the differences to identify gaps in my understanding.

question.en: How did you achieve a good result in this course?
question.zh: 你是如何在这门课中取得好成绩的

en: I did not rely on last-minute revision.
From the beginning, I tried to build a solid foundation in the basic concepts and develop a structured approach to weekly review.
I broke difficult chapters down into manageable parts and used exercises to identify gaps in my understanding.
When I remained unsure, I would seek clarification and feedback from the teacher or classmates.
zh: 我没有依靠考前突击。
从课程开始时，我就努力在基本概念方面打下扎实基础，并形成有条理的每周复习方法。
我会把困难章节拆分成容易处理的部分，再通过练习发现自己理解中的缺口。
如果仍有不确定的地方，我会向老师或同学主动寻求解释和反馈。

question.en: Which undergraduate course impressed you most, and why?
question.zh: 哪门本科课程给你的印象最深，为什么

en: One course that influenced me a lot was Operating Systems.
It was challenging because topics such as processes, memory management, and concurrency are closely connected.
I used mind maps to organize the concepts instead of memorizing them separately, and I achieved a good result in the course.
More importantly, it taught me to reason from mechanisms.
In system-level problems, a small misunderstanding can cause a large error, so the course also trained me to be more precise and systematic.
zh: 对我影响很大的一门课是操作系统。
它的难点在于进程、内存管理、并发等概念彼此联系很紧。
我后来用思维导图把知识结构串起来，而不是零散记忆，最后也取得了比较好的成绩。
更重要的是，这门课让我习惯从机制出发去理解问题。
系统层面的一个小误解可能造成很大的错误，所以它也训练了我的严谨性和系统思维。

question.en: How do you manage your time and stay organized?
question.zh: 你如何管理时间并保持条理

en: I use a simple rule: deadlines first, then the most important long-term task.
I break large tasks into small actions that can be finished in one sitting, because vague tasks are easy to postpone.
I also set a minimum daily goal.
On a difficult day, finishing the minimum keeps the project moving.
At the end of the day, I review what actually took time and adjust the next plan instead of making an overly detailed schedule.
zh: 我的方法比较简单：先处理有截止时间的事情，再保证最重要的长期任务持续推进。
我会把大任务拆成一次可以完成的小动作，因为模糊任务最容易拖延。
同时我会设一个每天的最低目标，状态不好时至少完成这个最低量。
晚上再根据实际耗时调整第二天计划，而不是把日程表做得过度精细。

question.en: Could you describe your study habits and learning methods?
question.zh: 请描述你的学习习惯和方法

en: When I learn a difficult topic, I first try to build a structure rather than memorize details.
For example, in Operating Systems I used mind maps to connect processes, memory management, and concurrency.
After I understand the structure, I use exercises or small implementations to test whether I really understand it.
I also explain the idea in my own words.
If I cannot explain it simply, I usually have not understood it well enough yet.
zh: 学习难点内容时，我会先搭知识结构，而不是先背细节。
例如学习操作系统时，我用思维导图把进程、内存管理和并发串起来。
理解结构后，再通过题目或小实现检查自己是否真的掌握，并尝试用自己的话解释。
如果一个概念我还不能简单讲清楚，通常说明理解还不够。
